content:
Here is a two-second party trick: the cube of a number ending in 2 always ends in 8, and vice versa. The whole chapter runs on patterns like that — and the IMO checks who has actually internalised them. Take the free IMO Class 8 Cube Roots online test below before any revision. Ten MCQs, instant score, full explanations — it will tell you exactly what to fix first.

What the IMO asks from Cube Roots in Class 8

  • Recognising perfect cubes; unit-digit reasoning.
  • Smallest multiplier or divisor to reach a perfect cube.
  • Cube roots by prime factorisation (triples, not pairs).
  • Estimating cube roots by grouping the last three digits.
  • Hardy–Ramanujan-style two-way sums and cube patterns.

Key facts and formulas to revise first

  • Unit digits swap in fixed pairs: 2 ↔ 8 and 3 ↔ 7; every other digit keeps its own.
  • A perfect cube needs every prime factor in a group of THREE — 500 = 2² × 5³ fails on the 2s.
  • 1729 = 1³ + 12³ = 9³ + 10³ — the smallest number expressible as two cube-sums.
  • Grouping digits: for 12167, the last three digits end in 7, so the cube root ends in 3.

Mistakes that cost Olympiad marks

  • Pairing prime factors (square habit) when cubes need triples.
  • Multiplying by 2 when dividing by 2 would reach the cube faster — read the question.
  • Assuming ∛(a + b) equals ∛a + ∛b.

quiz.title: IMO Class 8 Cube Roots Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.
quiz.about: IMO Maths Olympiad Class 8: Cubes and Cube Roots

questions.q: Which of the following numbers is a perfect cube?
questions.explanation: 216 = 6³ = 6 × 6 x 6. To verify: 6 × 6 = 36, 36 × 6 = 216. The other numbers cannot be expressed as the cube of any integer (200 = 2³ x 5², 250 = 2 × 5³, 300 = 2² x 3 × 5² -- none have all exponents divisible by 3).

questions.q: What is the units digit of 17³?
questions.explanation: The units digit of a cube depends only on the units digit of the base. Units digit of 17 is 7. Now 7³ = 343, whose units digit is 3. (Verify: 17³ = 4913, units digit 3.)

questions.q: The smallest natural number by which 72 must be multiplied to make it a perfect cube is:
questions.explanation: Prime factorise 72: 72 = 2³ x 3². For a perfect cube, every prime factor's exponent must be a multiple of 3. The exponent of 2 is already 3. The exponent of 3 is 2, which needs 1 more to become 3. So multiply by 3¹ = 3.
(-4)³ = (-4) × (-4) × (-4). First: (-4) × (-4) = 16. Then 16 × (-4) = -64. The cube of a negative number is always negative.

questions.q: The sum of cubes of the first 4 natural numbers (1³ + 2³ + 3³ + 4³) equals:
questions.explanation: 1³ + 2³ + 3³ + 4³ = 1 + 8 + 27 + 64 = 100. Note that this equals (1 + 2 + 3 + 4)² = 10² = 100, illustrating the identity: the sum of cubes of first n natural numbers equals the square of their sum.
(-10)³ = (-10) × (-10) × (-10) = 100 × (-10) = -1000. The cube of a negative number is always negative.

questions.q: Given 13824 = 2⁹ x 3³, the value of ∛(13824) is:
If the volume of a cube is 64 cm³, its total surface area is:
questions.explanation: Edge = ∛(64) = 4 cm. Total surface area of a cube = 6 x edge² = 6 × 16 = 96 cm².
